messages:
mike: Quick heads-up — seeing revoke ops surface on billing as org-owner instead of the service-account project after yesterday’s routing change. Anyone tracking attribution differences?

anya: Yup. Intermittent, mostly when console does the short-lived exchange and the call gets routed through the auth-proxy. Project claim missing downstream.

mike: The router change increased proxy-path volume so this noise became visible in quota dashboards.

dex: Two immediate fixes: (1) API fallback that checks authn-cache for last effective project for the token id, (2) Console attach signed X-Origin-Project header on revoke requests so proxy can't drop it.

anya: Agreed. For medium term we should cryptographically bind project to token (token_v2 with claim `pjt`) — avoids header fragility. Needs migration though.

ops-bot: action: create incident INC-2026-revoke-attr (P2). Add rollback: revert routing change.

mike: Also want a short-lived metric: `auth_attrib_fallback_total` + Grafana panel under Console/Billing so support can see token|fallback|proxy split.

design: UX idea: add revoke confirmation line: "Revoking as: service-account X (project Y) — charges billed to project Y". Low-friction, reduces tickets.

dex: Plan: canary API fallback now; console header PR in parallel; metric + panel; schedule token_v2 work for Q2. Backfill job to reclassify last 48h telemetry after fallback.

mike: Sounds good. I'll monitor the canary and page if fallback_rate > 0.3% of revokes. :thumbsup:
